decoded.meaning: SETTINGS{ NAME "flatten_dropped" VALUE u64=0, NAME "forward_iov_dropped" VALUE u64=0, NAME "arena_dropped" VALUE u64=0, NAME "assemble_dropped" VALUE u64=0, NAME "reply_iov_dropped" VALUE u64=0, NAME "delivery_iov_dropped" VALUE u64=0, NAME "malformed_rx" VALUE u64=0 } — the NET-PLANE router seam, as `read <any-vertex>:stats.router.drops` answers it on a node whose router has forwarded nothing (RFC-0010 Amendment 2 §D.4, #1503 residual)
decoded.note: bytes emitted by the libtracer reference encoder. The block shape is Amendment 1 §D.3's, unchanged — one READ is one SEAM is one BLOCK, NAME/VALUE pairs in the declaration order of the underlying POD, each a FIXED-WIDTH u64 little-endian, readers MUST ignore unknown NAMEs. What Amendment 2 adds is WHERE the block comes from: the counters are per-`fwd_router_t`, so L4 cannot reach them, and the router instead registers a sampler UP into the graph (`graph_t::configure_stats_sampler`) alongside the five {fn, ctx} seams its constructor already installs. A node with NO router constructed publishes no net-plane seam at all: `:stats.router.drops`, `:stats.labels.table` and every `:stats.link.<child>` answer ERROR{0x0031 tr::schema::not_found}, which per Amendment 1 §Compatibility a monitor MUST read as 'this node does not publish that seam'. The same answer covers a link sub-key that names no registered child, and one whose child has been removed.
